title: Transport and Congestion
description: Reliability, windows, and how senders share a pipe they cannot see. TCP first; QUIC as a later design that learned the same lessons.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS144
sourceReferences.notes: Labs build a reliable transport. Congestion is a mechanism, not a slogan.

sourceReferences.title: TCP Congestion Control
sourceReferences.notes: Slow start, AIMD, fast retransmit as sender mechanisms.

sourceReferences.title: QUIC
sourceReferences.notes: Transport over UDP so the protocol can change without the kernel.

modules.title: Reliability
learningObjectives: Retransmit what was lost so a byte stream can be rebuilt
Treat TCP states and windows as mechanism, not a flag list

modules.title: Congestion control
learningObjectives: Share a pipe the sender cannot see
Separate congestion of the path from a receiver that is full

modules.title: Modern transports
learningObjectives: Treat delay, marks, and user-space transports as later answers to the same problem
Name the middlebox as part of the path

concepts.name: Reliable delivery
concepts.summary: Retransmit what was lost, in order, exactly once — approximately.
objectives: Explain reliable delivery as retransmitting what was lost so the receiver sees each byte once, in order — approximately
Predict what sequence numbers and acknowledgements let a sender decide to retransmit

concepts.name: TCP state machine
concepts.summary: LISTEN to TIME_WAIT as a protocol, not a diagram to memorize.
objectives: Describe TCP connection states as protocol rules, not a diagram to memorize
Predict why TIME_WAIT exists after a close

concepts.name: The handshake
concepts.summary: Three packets to agree a starting sequence.
objectives: Explain the three-way handshake as agreeing a starting sequence in each direction
Predict what is known after SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK that was not known before

concepts.name: Sliding windows
concepts.summary: Many packets in flight, one window to bound them.
objectives: Describe a sliding window as many packets in flight bounded by one window
Predict how much data can be in flight given a window and a bandwidth-delay product

concepts.name: Flow control
concepts.summary: The receiver advertising how much it can still take.
objectives: Explain flow control as the receiver advertising how much it can still take
Distinguish a receiver that is full from a path that is congested

concepts.name: Retransmit timers
concepts.summary: When silence means loss.
objectives: Explain a retransmit timer as treating silence as loss
Predict the cost of a timer that is much shorter or much longer than the real RTT

concepts.name: Fast retransmit
concepts.summary: Triple-duplicate ACK as an earlier hint than a timeout.
objectives: Describe fast retransmit as using triple-duplicate ACKs as an earlier loss hint than a timeout
Predict why duplicate ACKs appear when a packet is lost but later packets arrive

concepts.name: Nagle and delayed ACK
concepts.summary: Two optimizations that deadlock each other.
objectives: Explain Nagle and delayed ACK as two optimizations that can stall each other
Predict a deadlock-like pause when both a small send and a delayed ACK wait for the other

concepts.name: Keepalives
concepts.summary: Probing a quiet connection so middleboxes do not forget it.
objectives: Describe a keepalive as probing a quiet connection so the path does not forget it
Predict why a long-idle connection can vanish without keepalives

concepts.name: Congestion control
concepts.summary: How senders share a pipe they cannot see.
objectives: Explain congestion control as how senders share a pipe they cannot see
Predict why a sender must infer path capacity from feedback rather than being told

concepts.name: AIMD
concepts.summary: Additive increase, multiplicative decrease — fairness from a rule.
objectives: Describe AIMD as additive increase and multiplicative decrease
Predict how two senders using the same AIMD rule share a bottleneck

concepts.name: Slow start
concepts.summary: Exponential probing until you hit something.
objectives: Explain slow start as exponential probing until a signal is hit
Predict why slow start grows the window faster than AIMD's additive increase

concepts.name: RTT estimation
concepts.summary: Jacobson/Karels: the mean is not enough; you need the variance.
objectives: Explain RTT estimation as needing both a mean and a variance
Predict why a timeout based only on the mean is too aggressive when delay varies

concepts.name: TCP fairness
concepts.summary: Equal shares among equal RTTs — and the bias when they are not.
objectives: Describe TCP fairness as equal shares among equal RTTs
Predict the bias when two flows share a bottleneck but have different RTTs

concepts.name: Head-of-line blocking
concepts.summary: One lost packet stalling the streams behind it.
objectives: Explain head-of-line blocking as one lost packet stalling the streams behind it
Predict why a reliable ordered byte stream delays later independent messages

concepts.name: Bufferbloat
concepts.summary: Huge buffers turning loss into delay.
objectives: Describe bufferbloat as huge buffers turning congestion into delay instead of honest loss
Predict why a latency-sensitive flow suffers in a standing queue even when the link is not dropping

concepts.name: Explicit congestion notification
concepts.summary: Marking instead of dropping.
objectives: Explain ECN as marking a packet instead of dropping it
Predict what a sender should do when it sees a congestion mark

concepts.name: Delay-based control (BBR)
concepts.summary: Model the pipe instead of waiting for a drop.
objectives: Describe delay-based control as modeling the pipe instead of waiting for a drop
Contrast a loss-based reaction with one that uses delay and delivery rate

concepts.name: QUIC
concepts.summary: Transport over UDP so we can change it without the kernel.
objectives: Explain QUIC as a transport over UDP so it can change without the kernel
Predict how QUIC avoids head-of-line blocking across independent streams

concepts.name: Where TLS sits
concepts.summary: Encryption as a layer, and why QUIC ate it.
objectives: Locate TLS as encryption sitting on a byte stream, and say why QUIC absorbed it
Predict what a middlebox that only understands TCP plus TLS cannot see inside QUIC

concepts.name: When UDP is the right tool
concepts.summary: Media, games, and anything that would rather drop than stall.
objectives: Explain when UDP is the right tool: anything that would rather drop than stall
Predict why a media sender often prefers a late packet dropped to a reliable stall

concepts.name: Middleboxes
concepts.summary: The path is not just routers. It rewrites you.
objectives: Describe a middlebox as a device on the path that rewrites or filters, not just a router
Predict why an unexpected header or a quiet flow can be dropped or rewritten
